# Fixed render fingerprints v1

`render_regression_v1.json` contains SHA-256 fingerprints only: no PDFs, extracted
statement text, account data, or original source snapshots. Inputs are the existing
fictional examples/replay data plus deterministic synthetic stress rows. Input
hashes detect accidental changes to those sources. Historical parity baselines and
the eight USBank Mac GOLDENS are not regenerated by this tool.

## Contract

- Four variants: Chase personal/business, USBank personal/business.
- Each covers default, empty, multipage/stress, replay, with watermark on and off
  (32 cases per profile). Chase personal's historical engine is fixed to two pages;
  its stress case exercises overflow into the second page, not arbitrary pagination.
- Per page: UTF-8 extracted text SHA-256, length-framed decompressed content-stream
  SHA-256, RGB 72 dpi pixel SHA-256, page rectangle and pixel dimensions.
- PDF bytes, timestamps, metadata, encryption randomness, xref IDs and compressed
  byte representation are deliberately outside this contract.
- Capture requires original P4 source directories. It first compares every field
  of every current case against the corresponding original-source rendering, then
  saves only the fingerprints and original source-file SHA-256 provenance.

## Renderer and platform profiles

A profile binds exact PyMuPDF, MuPDF, Pillow and FreeType versions and SHA-256 of
all four resolved donor font files. Platform names are informational; identical
resources may share a profile across operating systems. Mac Arial and Debian
Liberation Sans are distinct profiles. Embedded fonts alone do not guarantee
portability: Chase extends Type3 glyphs using the resolved bold font; USBank
business can transplant glyphs from resolved donor fonts. Chase prepared assets
are rebuilt in an isolated temporary cache for each module/process, never reused
from another platform and never written to the source tree by this tool.

Both committed profiles were independently compared against the unchanged P4
source snapshots: macOS Arial and Linux Debian Liberation, PyMuPDF 1.26.6 /
MuPDF 1.26.11 / Pillow 13.0.0 (see exact FreeType/font hashes in JSON). Linux was
captured using the project's Docker Debian runtime. This is not a promise that
Ubuntu/macOS font packages or a different renderer version produce equal pixels.

`python tools/render_regression.py check` is the strict CI command. An unknown
profile fails explicitly; it never replaces a fixed check with a self-comparison.
Ordinary pytest reports unknown-profile tests as explicit skips so broader Python
and OS matrices can still test mechanics. CI must run the strict command in the
pinned Docker runtime as a separate required job. A dependency/font upgrade needs
review and a fresh original-source capture, not an automatic baseline overwrite:

```
python tools/render_regression.py capture \
  --chase-original /temporary/untouched/chase \
  --usbank-original /temporary/untouched/usbank
```

CapitalOne's CJK fallback is selected from OS fonts. Its existing subset-vs-full
font tests compare text, glyphs, content, fonts, metadata and pixels within one
environment; no Mac-specific C1 pixel hash is imposed on Linux.
